I couldn't confirm anything on disk. Every shell call I made returned no output, including a plain `echo`, so I could not read `/home/dev/380118/app`, check whether `notes/` exists, or write the file. The notes and declarations below come from the copies you pasted into the message.

The answers come from notes 6, 34, 56 and 70 of `camera-notes.md`:

- **(a) resolves.** Note 6 says a change before the first frame becomes the start, and that first frame zeroes inertia, so the flick's coasting is absorbed and the transition runs to completion. One thing I can't check from the notes: if attachControl's frame hook runs after interpolate's first frame in the same tick, it could add the offset one last time and cause a rejection. That depends on hook ordering the notes don't describe.
- **(b) rejects.** A mouse drag writes `inertialAlphaOffset` and `inertialBetaOffset` (note 70), and the frame hook adds those to alpha and beta each frame. That is a change by something other than interpolate between its frames (note 6).
- **(c) rejects.** Note 6 explicitly includes a second call on the camera, so the first call's promise rejects when the second call changes the pose.

The file to create at `app/notes/go-home.json`:

FILE: app/notes/go-home.json
```json
{
  "a": "resolves",
  "b": "rejects",
  "c": "rejects"
}
```

Once the tools work again, the next step is to confirm the directory exists and write this file. Then add a try/catch around `goHome()` that treats a rejection as "superseded or interrupted" in cases (b) and (c), and treats a resolve in (a) as normal completion.
